source.title: On the generic part of the cohomology of compact unitary Shimura varieties
readSections: The published Annals PDF, read in full: 118 pages, pp. 649–766, SHA-256 4f9449e5ecfd8fb8b43a04acef73060f531be995babaa9f744f3db36aaa5e61a, fetched from https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v186-n3-p01-p.pdf on 23 September 2026 (received 19 November 2015, accepted 5 April 2017, published online 12 September 2017). Item locators are journal pages. arXiv 1511.02418 has only v1 (8 November 2015, 96 pages, SHA-256 aa93df3947e57ab78b070a82d638e70c25ae2ae15aeb60346575e74fdf85b349), a pre-referee version; it was consulted for the bibliography and for which recorded mistakes it already contains.

Cited inputs were not read; items resting on Scholze [Sch15a], [Sch13a]–[Sch13d] and the Lubin–Tate tower paper, Scholze–Weinstein [SW13], Kedlaya–Liu [KL15], Fargues [Far15a], Fargues–Fontaine [FF14], Rapoport–Zink [RZ96], Rapoport–Richartz [RR96], Kottwitz [Kot84], [Kot85], [Kot90], [Kot92a], [Kot92b], Mantovan [Man05], Hamacher [Ham15], Oort–Zink [OZ02], Berthelot [Ber80], Shin [Shi09]–[Shi12], Chenevier–Harris [CH13], Caraiani [Car12], Badulescu [Bad07], Labesse [Lab91], [Lab99], Arthur [Art88a], [Art88b], [Art89], Illusie [Ill94], Huber [Hub96], Milne [Mil90], Blasius [Bla94], Kisin [Kis10] and Deligne [DMOS82] state them as the paper uses them.

summary: Caraiani and Scholze prove that for compact unitary Shimura varieties (Kottwitz's simple ones, or those quasi-split at all finite places) the F_ℓ-cohomology localized at a Hecke eigensystem m is concentrated in the middle degree, and the Z_ℓ-cohomology torsion-free there, provided ρ_m is decomposed generic at the places above some prime p split in F (Theorems 1.1, 6.3.1); on the way they attach ρ_m to such m. The method works at an auxiliary p ≠ ℓ with the Hodge–Tate period map π_HT : S_{K^p} → Fℓ_{G,µ}: they refine it for Hodge type (it lands in Fℓ_{G,µ} and pulls back automorphic bundles), stratify Fℓ_{G,µ} by B(G, µ^{-1}) through modifications of G-bundles on the Fargues–Fontaine curve (the µ-ordinary stratum closed, the basic one open), identify the fibres of π_HT over the b-stratum with perfect Igusa varieties via Rapoport–Zink spaces at infinite level, show that the nearby cycles of Rπ_HT*F_ℓ are perverse, and use Shin's trace formula for Igusa varieties with base change to show that only the µ-ordinary stratum survives genericity. The atlas's Igusa roadmap builds this machinery for the non-compact sequel; the compact endgame goes to a proposed Part II of it, the general-PEL Igusa, Rapoport–Zink and perversity material is a source of IG.0–IG.4, the flag-variety Newton strata of BG2–BG3, the Bialynicki-Birula isomorphism of GS0, the relative Hodge–Tate filtration of P8 and Scholze–Weinstein's p-divisible groups of T0/T2. Thirteen misprints are recorded.

items.name: Theorem 1.1 (the generic part of torsion cohomology is concentrated in the middle degree)
items.statement: Let G be an anisotropic unitary similitude group of dimension n for a CM field F containing an imaginary quadratic field, of Kottwitz's simple type (associated with a division algebra over F) or quasi-split at all finite places (§5.1). For a system of Hecke eigenvalues m appearing in H^i(X_Γ, F_ℓ) there is an associated ρ_m : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(F̄_ℓ). If some rational prime p is completely decomposed in F and ρ_m is unramified and decomposed generic at every place of F above p, then i = q_0 is the middle degree.
items.note: Precise form: Theorem 6.3.1. Remark 1.2: the Galois representation also follows from [Sch15a], by a different proof; Remark 1.5: for signature (0, n) at all but one infinite place (Harris–Taylor case) one decomposed generic place suffices.

items.name: Remarks 1.3 and 1.7.1 (integral and twisted coefficients)
items.statement: If the conclusion of Theorem 1.1 holds, the Z_ℓ-cohomology localized at m is concentrated in degree q_0 and torsion-free; by Hochschild–Serre and Poincaré duality the theorem also holds for a nontrivial Hecke-equivariant coefficient system in place of F_ℓ.
items.note: Stated as formal consequences.

items.name: Definition 1.9 = Definition 6.2.1 (decomposed generic)
items.statement: For a p-adic field L with residue field F_q and ℓ ≠ p, an unramified ρ : Gal(L̄/L) → GL_n(F̄_ℓ) is decomposed generic if the eigenvalues λ_1, …, λ_n of ρ(Frob), Frob an arithmetic Frobenius, satisfy λ_i/λ_j ∉ {1, q} for i ≠ j. The condition depends only on the semisimplification and forces ρ to be semisimple.
items.note: IG.5/IG.7 use the related condition α_i ≠ pα_j for CSnc's non-compact datum.

items.name: Normalization of covariant Dieudonné theory
items.statement: Covariant Dieudonné modules with Frobenius divided by p: µ_{p^∞} ↦ (Z_p, F = p^{-1}), Q_p/Z_p ↦ (Z_p, F = 1), slopes in [−1, 0]; the isocrystal (Q_p, F = p^{-1}) goes to O(1) on the Fargues–Fontaine curve, so slopes of p-divisible groups and of their bundles agree; µ = µ_h is the standard Hodge cocharacter and Newton strata are indexed by B(G, µ^{-1}).
items.locator: §1, Notation and conventions, p. 659; §4.1, p. 692 (footnote 18), Example 4.1.3
items.note: R07.2 plans Dieudonné modules 'in the covariant or contravariant convention chosen'; VB0 pins the slope convention of isocrystals and bundles.

items.name: Shimura data, the Hodge cocharacter, the parabolics P_µ, P^std_µ and the flag varieties
items.statement: For a Shimura datum (G, X), µ = µ_h, P^std_µ = {g : lim_{t→∞} ad(µ(t))g exists} (stabilizer of the descending filtration Fil^•(µ)), P_µ the opposite parabolic (stabilizer of the ascending Fil_•(µ)), M_µ = Cent_G(µ); flag varieties Fl^std_{G,µ} and Fl_{G,µ} over the reflex field E; the holomorphic Borel embedding X ↪ Fl^std_{G,µ}(C) and the antiholomorphic X ↪ Fl_{G,µ}(C).
items.note: D3 plans the parabolic stabilizing the Hodge filtration, the compact dual as a flag variety and the Borel embedding.

items.name: Hodge-type Shimura varieties and Siegel embeddings (Example 2.1.1)
items.statement: The Siegel datum (GSp(V, ψ), X̃) with S̃_K̃ the moduli of principally polarized abelian varieties with level structure; Hodge type means an embedding (G, X) ↪ (G̃, X̃), giving closed embeddings Fl^{(std)}_{G,µ} ↪ Fl^{(std)}_{G̃,µ̃} and S_K ↪ S̃_K̃ ⊗ E for suitable K̃ [Del71, Prop. 1.15].
items.note: V6 plans Hodge- and abelian-type canonical models; PELModuli M1–M2 the Siegel moduli problem.

items.name: Theorem 2.1.2 (Scholze: perfectoid Shimura varieties of Hodge type)
items.statement: For small K^p there is a perfectoid space S_{K^p} over E_p with S_{K^p} ~ lim_{K_p} (S_{K^pK_p} ⊗ E_p)^ad, and a G(Q_p)-equivariant Hodge–Tate period map π_HT : S_{K^p} → Fℓ_{G̃,µ̃}, equivariant for the G(A^p_f)-Hecke action with trivial action on the target; on points it sends (A, T_pA ≅ Z_p^{2g}) to the Hodge–Tate filtration Lie(A) ⊂ C^{2g}. Every point of Fℓ has affinoid open neighbourhoods U with π_HT^{-1}(U) affinoid perfectoid and the preimage of an affinoid at finite level [Sch15a, Thm IV.1.1(i)].
items.locator: §2.1, Theorem 2.1.2, p. 662; §6.1, proof of Proposition 6.1.3, p. 752
items.note: Part of [Sch15a, Thm IV.1.1]. S1–S2 plan the Siegel and Hodge-type perfectoid towers, S3 the Hodge–Tate period map.

items.name: Theorem 1.10 = Theorem 2.1.3(1) (π_HT factors through Fℓ_{G,µ})
items.statement: For Hodge-type data the Hodge–Tate period map of S_{K^p} factors through Fℓ_{G,µ} ↪ Fℓ_{G̃,µ̃}, independently of the Siegel embedding, and is functorial in the Shimura datum.
items.note: T2 plans 'for Hodge type prove that the tensor conditions cut out the expected flag variety'; S3 constructs the period map on the Hodge-type tower.

items.name: Theorem 2.1.3(2) (automorphic vector bundles are pulled back along π_HT)
items.statement: For µ fixed over a finite extension of E, the tensor functor f_p : Rep M_µ ↪ Rep P_µ → {G(Q_p)-equivariant bundles on Fℓ_{G,µ}} →π_HT^* {G(Q_p)-equivariant bundles on S_{K^p}} is isomorphic to f_∞ : Rep M_µ ↪ Rep P^std_µ → {automorphic vector bundles on S_K} → {bundles on S_{K^p}}, Hecke-equivariantly and independently of the Siegel embedding (Remark 2.1.4: canonically, via G-equivariant bundles on the space of cocharacters).
items.locator: §2.1, Theorem 2.1.3(2), Remark 2.1.4, pp. 662–663; proof: Lemmas 2.3.5, 2.3.8, Proposition 2.3.9, pp. 670–674
items.note: S3 plans the pullback identification of the Levi torsor and its automorphic bundles; T2 the comparison of the Hodge–Tate Levi torsor with the de Rham one.

items.name: Automorphic vector bundles and the standard principal bundle
items.statement: For ξ ∈ Rep P^std_µ, W(ξ) is the G_C-equivariant bundle on Fl^std_{G,µ} and V(ξ) := G(Q)\(W(ξ) × G(A_f)/K) on S_K(C), algebraic and defined over the field of definition of ξ; descent uses Milne's standard principal bundle G_dR → S_K with its map to Fl^std_{G,µ} [Mil90, §§III–IV, Prop. 3.5, Thms 4.1, 4.3].
items.note: B1 plans the canonical principal bundle, B2 automorphic bundles for representations of the parabolic/Levi. The proof of Lemma 2.3.5 writes G/P_µ and Fl_{G,µ} for G/P^std_µ and Fl^std_{G,µ} (sourceIssues E1).

items.name: Definition 2.2.1 and the structural de Rham sheaves
items.statement: On X_proét: Ô_X, Ô^+_{X♭} (inverse perfection of Ô^+/p), B^+_dR,X = completion of W(Ô^+_{X♭})[1/p] along ker θ, B_dR,X = B^+_dR,X[ξ^{-1}] with Fil^i = ξ^iB^+_dR and gr^0 = Ô_X; OB^+_dR,X, OB_dR,X with filtration and connection, (OB_dR)^{∇=0} = B_dR [Sch13c, §6].
items.note: P8:local-rational constructs the rational structural period sheaves and the relative Poincaré lemma.

items.name: Theorem 2.2.2 (Scholze: relative p-adic de Rham comparison)
items.statement: For π : X → S proper smooth between smooth adic spaces over a complete discretely valued K with perfect residue field, if R^iπ_*F_p is locally free on S_proét for all i, then R^iπ_*Ẑ_p is de Rham with associated filtered module with integrable connection R^iπ_dR*O_X, and R^iπ_*Ẑ_p ⊗ OB_dR,S ≅ R^iπ_dR*O_X ⊗ OB_dR,S compatibly with filtrations and connections [Sch13c, Thm 8.8].
items.note: Footnote 9: the local-freeness hypothesis holds for algebraizable π and was announced in general by Gabber. P8 applies CP.3–CP.4 to the proper-smooth comparison with connection.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.3 (Scholze: the two B^+_dR-lattices)
items.statement: With M = R^iπ_*Ẑ_p ⊗ B^+_dR,S and M_0 = (R^iπ_dR*O_X ⊗ OB^+_dR,S)^{∇=0}: M ⊗ B_dR ≅ M_0 ⊗ B_dR, M_0 ⊂ M, and (M ∩ Fil^jM_0)/(M ∩ Fil^{j+1}M_0) = (Fil^{−j}R^iπ_dR*O_X) ⊗ Ô_S(j) inside gr^jM_0 [Sch13c, Prop. 7.9].
items.note: The associatedness of de Rham local systems; P8.

items.name: The relative Hodge–Tate filtration and Corollary 2.2.4
items.statement: The ascending filtration on gr^0M = R^iπ_*Ẑ_p ⊗ Ô_S given by Fil_{−j} = (M ∩ Fil^jM_0)/(Fil^1M ∩ Fil^jM_0) (Fil_{−1} = 0, Fil_i everything); its graded pieces are gr_j(R^iπ_*Ẑ_p ⊗ Ô_S) ≅ (gr^jR^iπ_dR*O_X) ⊗ Ô_S(−j), and Fil_0 = R^iπ_*O_X ⊗ Ô_S.
items.note: Generalizes the degree-one Hodge–Tate filtration of [Sch15a] (and of [Sch13d, §3] over a point) to proper smooth families.

items.name: Proposition 2.2.5 (the first step of the relative Hodge–Tate filtration)
items.statement: Fil_0 of the relative Hodge–Tate filtration is the natural map R^iπ_*O_X ⊗ Ô_S → R^iπ_*Ô_X ≅ R^iπ_*Ẑ_p ⊗ Ô_S, which is injective.
items.note: Via the relative Poincaré lemma; the proof writes f for π.

items.name: Hodge tensors and the torsors of frames (Lemma 2.3.1)
items.statement: G ⊂ GSp(V, ψ) is the stabilizer of tensors (s_α) ⊂ V^⊗ [DMOS82, Prop. 3.1]; they give Hodge tensors s_α,B on the Betti local system V_B, and the G(Q)-torsor X × G(A_f)/K → S_K(C) is the torsor of isomorphisms V × U ≅ V_B|U respecting the tensors. A second embedding is related by an idempotent e ∈ V^⊗.
items.note: B1 plans the Hodge-type tensor description of the canonical principal bundle.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.2 and Remark 2.3.3 (Kisin, Deligne: de Rham and étale Hodge tensors are defined over E)
items.statement: The horizontal tensors s_α,dR ⊂ V_dR^⊗ (V_dR = (R^1π_dR*O_A)^∨) and the étale tensors s_α,p ⊂ V_p^⊗ are defined over the reflex field E; the isomorphism V'_dR ≅ e_dR V_dR^⊗ for a second embedding is defined over E.
items.note: [Kis10], via Deligne's theorem that Hodge cycles on abelian varieties are absolute Hodge [DMOS82]. B1 plans the absolute-Hodge and comparison statements; T1 the compatibility of Hodge tensors with the comparison maps.

items.name: Lemmas 2.3.4–2.3.5 (the de Rham torsors P_dR and M_dR)
items.statement: P_dR, the P^std_µ-torsor of frames of V_dR respecting the tensors and the Hodge filtration, is independent of the symplectic embedding; its pushout M_dR = P_dR ×^{P^std_µ} M_µ encodes the tensor functor f_∞ of Theorem 2.1.3.

items.name: Blasius: Hodge tensors under the p-adic comparison
items.statement: For an abelian variety over a number field, the de Rham and étale realizations of a Hodge tensor correspond under the Hodge–Tate and p-adic de Rham comparison isomorphisms [Bla94].
items.note: T1: 'For the Hodge-type application prove compatibility of Hodge tensors with the comparison maps.'

items.name: Lemmas 2.3.6–2.3.7 (the Hodge–Tate torsor P_p)
items.statement: P_p(U) = {β : V_p ⊗ Ô ≅ V ⊗ Ô | β(s_α,p ⊗ 1) = s_α ⊗ 1, β(Fil_•) = Fil_•(µ)} (relative Hodge–Tate filtration, completed structure sheaf) is a P_µ-torsor on (S_K)_proét, independent of the symplectic embedding; the associated G-torsor G_p has a canonical section over S_{K^p}, which defines π_HT.
items.note: T2 plans the Hodge–Tate parabolic reduction and Levi torsor on the pro-étale site.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.8 and Proposition 2.3.9 (M_dR ≅ M_p)
items.statement: The M_µ-torsor M_p = P_p ×^{P_µ} M_µ encodes f_p; there is a canonical isomorphism M_dR ≅ M_p of M_µ-torsors on (S_K)_proét, independent of the embedding, from gr^j(V_dR ⊗ Ô) ≅ gr_j(V_p ⊗ Ô)(j) (Corollary 2.2.4), [Bla94] and the trivialization Ô(1) ≅ Ô.
items.note: T2: 'compare its Levi torsor with the de Rham/Hodge torsor'.

items.name: Definition 3.1.1 (isocrystals over F̄_p)
items.statement: An isocrystal over F̄_p is a finite-dimensional L-vector space V, L = W(F̄_p)[1/p], with a σ-linear automorphism φ; its height is dim_L V.
items.note: Mathlib's `WittVector.Isocrystal` is a K(p, k)-vector space, K(p, k) = FractionRing (𝕎 k), with a Frobenius-semilinear equivalence; for k = F̄_p this is the definition. Mathlib classifies only the one-dimensional ones (`WittVector.isocrystal_classification`).

items.name: Dieudonné–Manin classification
items.statement: Every isocrystal over F̄_p is ⊕_λ V_λ^{⊕n_λ}, V_λ = (L^r, (0 1 …; p^s 0)σ) for λ = s/r in lowest terms, with the slope-λ subspaces uniquely determined.
items.note: VB0 plans the Dieudonné–Manin classification with the pinned slope convention (Mathlib has rank one).

items.name: Isocrystals with G-structure and the set B(G)
items.statement: B(G) is the set of σ-conjugacy classes b ↦ hbσ(h)^{-1} in G(L); an isocrystal with G-structure is an exact tensor functor Rep_{Q_p}G → Isoc; B(G) is in bijection with their isomorphism classes (B(GL_n) ↔ isocrystals of height n via b ↦ (L^n, bσ)); H^1(Q_p, G) ↪ B(G) as the classes with trivial ν [Kot85].
items.note: BG0 defines B(G) and compares it with G-isocrystals, and constructs J_b.

items.name: The Newton map, the Kottwitz map and B(G, µ) (Definition 3.1.2)
items.statement: The Newton map ν : B(G) → (X_*(G) ⊗ Q)^Γ_dom via slope homomorphisms ν_b ∈ Hom(D_L, G_L); κ : B(G) → π_1(G)_Γ (val_p det for GL_n), compatible via averaging [RR96, 1.13, Thm 1.15]; (ν, κ) is injective. b ⪯ b' iff ν_b ⪯ ν_b' (difference a nonnegative rational combination of positive coroots) and κ(b) = κ(b'). B(G, µ) = {b : ν_b ⪯ µ̄, κ(b) = µ♭} with µ̄ the Galois average and µ♭ the image of µ in π_1(G)_Γ.
items.note: BG1 plans κ, ν, the partial order and their functoriality.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.1 (the rational annuli Y_I are preperfectoid affinoids)
items.statement: For F complete algebraically closed of characteristic p, Y_(0,∞) = Spa(W(O_F), W(O_F)) ∖ (p[ϖ] = 0) with α(x) = log|[ϖ](x̃)|/log|p(x̃)|; for I = [s, r] rational, Y_I = Spa(R^{[s,r]}_F, R^{[s,r],+}_F) is a sheafy affinoid, R^{[s,r],+} the p-adic completion of the integral closure of W(O_F)[p/[ϖ^{1/r}], [ϖ^{1/s}]/p], and R^{[s,r]}_F ⊗̂ K is perfectoid for every perfectoid K/Q_p.
items.note: The Tau Ceti adic-spaces roadmap's Layer 6 constructs 𝒴 and its radius function; RF0:integral-Y proves the charts perfectoid after extension.

items.name: Definition 3.2.2 (the adic Fargues–Fontaine curve) and the point ∞
items.statement: X_F = Y_(0,∞)/ϕ^Z (ϕ properly discontinuous, α∘ϕ = pα); for F = C♭, θ : W(O_F) → O_C gives a closed point ∞ with residue field C and completed local ring B^+_dR,C.
items.note: Layer 6 and RF1 (quotient); RF2:untilts (untilts and de Rham completions).

items.name: Theorem 3.2.3 (Fargues–Fontaine: classification of vector bundles)
items.statement: V ↦ E(V) (pull back an isocrystal to Y_(0,∞) and descend) induces a bijection between isomorphism classes of isocrystals and of vector bundles on X_F; it is not an equivalence of categories (Remark 3.2.4; proved for the schematic curve, with GAGA [KL15], [Far15b]).
items.note: VB2:classification.

items.name: Definition 3.2.5 and Remark 3.2.6 (O(d), degree and slopes)
items.statement: O_{X_F}(d) is the bundle of the isocrystal (L, p^{-d}σ); Z ≅ Pic X_F, degree, slopes and Harder–Narasimhan filtrations; slopes of V and E(V) differ by a sign.
items.note: RF3 (O(1), sign conversion) and VB1 (degree, slope).

items.name: Theorem 3.2.7 (Fargues–Fontaine: the schematic curve)
items.statement: X_F = Proj ⊕_{d≥0} H^0(X_F, O(d)) is a regular noetherian scheme of dimension 1 with field of constants Q_p, closed points with residue fields C, C♭ ≅ F, and complements of closed points spectra of PIDs; vector bundles on X_F and on its scheme are equivalent ([KL15], [Far15b]).
items.note: VB2:ampleness.

items.name: Definition 3.2.8 and Theorem 3.2.9 (Fargues: G-bundles on the curve)
items.statement: A G-bundle on X_F is an exact tensor functor Rep_{Q_p}G → Bun_{X_F}; b ↦ E_b induces a bijection B(G) ≅ {G-bundles on X_F}/≅ [Far15a].
items.note: BG0 (Tannakian G-torsors) and BG2 (the bijection |Bun_G| → B(G)).

items.name: The Robba ring and Kedlaya–Liu's comparison with ϕ-modules
items.statement: R̃_F = lim_r H^0(Y_(0,r], O) (a Bézout domain, [KL15, L 4.2.6]); ϕ-modules are finite projective (hence free) R̃_F-modules with a ϕ-linear automorphism, and vector bundles on X_F are equivalent to ϕ-modules over R̃_F [KL15, Thm 6.3.12].
items.note: VB1 compares bundles with finite projective modules on annuli and Frobenius descent.

items.name: The relative Fargues–Fontaine curve (§3.3)
items.statement: For a perfectoid affinoid (R, R^+) of characteristic p: Y_(0,∞)(R, R^+) with its rational charts preperfectoid (Proposition 3.3.1), X(R, R^+) = Y/ϕ^Z (Definition 3.3.2), the scheme X(R) = Proj ⊕ H^0(O(d)) independent of R^+, relative GAGA [KL15, Thm 8.7.7] (Theorem 3.3.3) and the equivalence with ϕ-modules over the relative Robba ring R̃_R [KL15, Thms 6.3.12, 8.7.7] (Theorem 3.3.4).
items.note: RF0–RF1 (relative curve), RF3 (graded algebra), VB2:ampleness (algebraization), VB1 (annuli).

items.name: Kedlaya–Liu: semicontinuity of Newton polygons in families
items.statement: For a vector bundle on X(R, R^+) (equivalently a ϕ-module over R̃_R), the Newton polygon is semicontinuous on |Spa(R, R^+)| [KL15, Thm 7.4.5].
items.note: VB4 proves semicontinuity of the geometric HN polygon with the source's dominance convention.

items.name: Definitions 3.4.1–3.4.2 (the B^+_dR-affine Grassmannian and its Schubert cells)
items.statement: For perfectoid (R, R^+) over Q_p, B^+_dR,R is the ξ-adic completion of W(R♭+)[1/p]; Gr^{B_dR^+}_G(R, R^+) = G-torsors on Spec B^+_dR,R trivialized over Spec B_dR,R; over (C, O_C) the Cartan decomposition G(B_dR,C) = ⊔ G(B^+)µ(ξ)^{-1}G(B^+) defines the relative position µ(x) ∈ X_*(G)_dom, and Gr_{G,µ} ⊂ Gr_G ⊗ E is the locus of relative position µ at all points.
items.note: GS0:loop-geometry constructs L^+G, LG, the Grassmannian and Schubert cells (footnote 14: a nonstandard sign µ(ξ)^{-1}).

items.name: Proposition 3.4.3 (the Bialynicki-Birula map)
items.statement: There is a natural map π_{G,µ} : Gr_{G,µ} → Fℓ_{G,µ} = G/P_µ; for GL_n and µ = (k_1 ≥ … ≥ k_n) a lattice Λ ⊂ B^n_dR,R gives the ascending filtration Fil_mR^n = ((B^+)^n ∩ ξ^{-m}Λ)/((ξB^+)^n ∩ ξ^{-m}Λ), with R^n/Fil_m finite projective by [KL15, Prop. 2.8.4].
items.note: GS0:Schubert-smoothness identifies a Schubert cell by its parabolic flag base and positive-loop unipotent fibres (footnote 15 on the sign of Fil_•(µ)).

items.name: Lemma 3.4.4 (the Bialynicki-Birula map on field points)
items.statement: For µ minuscule and (K, K^+) a perfectoid field over E, π_{G,µ} is bijective on (K, K^+)-points.
items.note: B^+_dR,K ≅ K[[ξ]] (Cohen); the classical affine Grassmannian [NP01, Lemme 6.2].

items.name: Lemma 3.4.6 (lattices are detected pointwise)
items.statement: Let Λ be a finite projective B^+_dR,R-module and a ∈ Λ ⊗ B_dR,R. If a ∈ Λ ⊗ B^+_dR,K(z) for every z ∈ Spa(R, R^+), then a ∈ Λ.
items.note: R is reduced.

items.name: Theorem 3.4.5 (for minuscule µ the Bialynicki-Birula map is an isomorphism)
items.statement: If µ is minuscule, π_{G,µ} : Gr^{B_dR^+}_{G,µ} → Fℓ_{G,µ} is an isomorphism.
items.note: Injectivity by Lemmas 3.4.4 and 3.4.6; surjectivity: Gr is a pro-étale sheaf ([KL15, §9.2, Thm 9.2.15]) and a B^+_dR-local system is built from the filtered module (V ⊗ O, ∇, Fil^{−•}), Griffiths transversal because µ is minuscule ([Del79, 1.1.14]), by [Sch13c, Prop. 7.9].

items.name: Theorem 3.5.1 (Kedlaya–Liu: Beauville–Laszlo gluing on the curve)
items.statement: Vector bundles on X(R♭) (or X(R♭, R♭+)) are equivalent to triples (M_1 on X(R♭) ∖ Z, M_2 on Spec B^+_dR,R, ι over Spec B_dR,R), Z the image of i_∞ : Spec R → X(R♭), compatibly with tensor products and exact sequences [KL15, Thm 8.9.6].
items.note: RF4:vector-bundles proves Beauville–Laszlo gluing along the untilt divisors.

items.name: Corollary 3.5.2 (the G-bundle of a point of the Grassmannian)
items.statement: E : Gr^{B_dR^+}_G(R, R^+) → {G-bundles on X(R♭, R♭+)} by modifying the trivial G-bundle along ∞; over (C, O_C) this gives b(·) : Gr_G(C, O_C) → B(G).
items.note: RF4:G-torsors transfers the gluing to G-torsors for GS0/BG2.

items.name: Lemma 3.5.4 (Newton above Hodge for modifications)
items.statement: For a rank-n bundle E on X_{C♭} trivialized off ∞ with relative position µ(E) from the trivial bundle, its Newton polygon ν_E (slopes of E ≅ ⊕ O(λ_i)) satisfies ν_E ⪯ µ(E); equivalently b(E) ∈ B(GL_n, µ(E)^{-1}) (footnote 17).
items.note: After Katz [Kat79]: top exterior power (a line bundle given by ξ^{-d}B^+_dR is O(d)) and the first slope (O^n ↪ E; no nonzero map O → O(λ) for λ < 0 [FF14]).

items.name: Lemma 3.5.5 (the Kottwitz invariant of a modification)
items.statement: κ ∘ b : Gr^{B_dR^+}_{G,µ}(C, O_C) → B(G) → π_1(G)_Γ is constant, equal to −µ♭.
items.note: z-extension G̃ with simply connected derived group [Kot85, 5.6] and the Cartan decomposition; then tori, induced tori Res_{K/Q_p}G_m (π_1 torsion-free [Kot85, L 2.2]), the norm and G_m (Lemma 3.5.4).

items.name: Proposition 3.5.3 (modifications of type µ land in B(G, µ^{-1}))
items.statement: For any reductive G over Q_p and any conjugacy class µ (not necessarily minuscule), x ∈ Gr^{B_dR^+}_{G,µ}(C, O_C) has b(E(x)) ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}).
items.note: Lemma 3.5.4 via [RR96, Lemma 2.2] for ν, Lemma 3.5.5 for κ.

items.name: Definition 3.5.6 (the Newton stratification of the flag variety)
items.statement: For minuscule µ, E : Fℓ_{G,µ}(R, R^+) ≅ Gr_{G,µ}(R, R^+) → {G-bundles on X(R♭, R♭+)} (Theorem 3.4.5); |Fℓ_{G,µ}| → B(G) sends a (C, C^+)-point to the class of E(x), independently of C; Fℓ^b_{G,µ} is the fibre over b. The map factors through the maximal Hausdorff quotient, the Berkovich space Fℓ^Berk_{G,µ}.
items.note: Higher-rank points have the image of their rank-one generalization.

items.name: Proposition 3.5.7 (semicontinuity and admissibility)
items.statement: (1) b(·) : |Fℓ_{G,µ}| → B(G) is lower semicontinuous; (2) its image lies in B(G, µ^{-1}).
items.note: (2) is Proposition 3.5.3; (1) on a pro-étale cover by an affinoid perfectoid, via representations [RR96, L 2.2] and [KL15, Thm 7.4.5]. The proof cites 'Corollary 3.3.4' for Theorem 3.3.4 (sourceIssues E2).

items.name: Remark 3.5.8 (Rapoport: every µ^{-1}-admissible class occurs)
items.statement: The image of |Fℓ_{G,µ}| → B(G, µ^{-1}) is all of B(G, µ^{-1}) [Rap15, Prop. A.9].
items.note: Rapoport's appendix to Scholze's Lubin–Tate tower paper, based on this section.

items.name: Theorem 1.11 = Corollary 3.5.9 (the strata are locally closed)
items.statement: Fℓ_{G,µ} = ⊔_{b∈B(G,µ^{-1})} Fℓ^b_{G,µ} with locally closed strata; Fℓ^{⪰b}_{G,µ} := ⊔_{b⪯b'} Fℓ^{b'}_{G,µ} is closed for every b; the basic stratum is open. The closure relations are opposite to those of Newton strata on Shimura varieties; the µ-ordinary stratum is closed.
items.note: Examples (§1): for the modular curve Fℓ = P^1 = P^1(Q_p) ⊔ Ω^2; for a nonsplit inner form of GL_5 with µ = (1,1,0,0,0) all classical points are basic. Footnote 6: the closure of a stratum is not shown to be a union of strata.

items.name: Tate modules and universal covers of p-divisible groups (Definition 4.1.1)
items.statement: For G a p-divisible group over a p-adically complete R, viewed as an fpqc sheaf on Nilp^op_R: T_p(G) = lim G[p^n] = Hom(Q_p/Z_p, G) and the universal cover G̃ = lim_p G = Hom(Q_p/Z_p, G)[1/p], a sheaf of Q_p-vector spaces, with 0 → T_pG → G̃ → G → 0.
items.note: Following [SW13, §3].

items.name: Proposition 4.1.2 (Messing, Scholze–Weinstein: representability of universal covers)
items.statement: (1) A connected G is an affine formal scheme with finitely generated ideal of definition, Spf R[[x_1, …, x_r]] if Lie G is free of rank r; (2) an isogeny induces G̃_1 ≅ G̃_2; for R perfect of characteristic p, G connected and Lie G free of rank r: (3) G̃ ≅ Spf R[[x_i^{1/p^∞}]] and (4) T_pG ≅ Spec R[[x_i^{1/p^∞}]]/(x_1, …, x_r).

items.name: Crystalline Dieudonné theory: M(G) and D(G)
items.statement: The Lie algebra of the universal vector extension of G [Mes72] made into a crystal M(G) [BBM82]; D(G) = M(G)(W(F̄_p) → F̄_p) with D(G) ⊂ ϕ_G(D(G)) ⊂ p^{-1}D(G); isoclinic of slope λ when the isocrystal has slope −λ.
items.note: R07.2 (Dieudonné theory) and R07.6 (Grothendieck–Messing). The text calls D(G)[1/p] an isocrystal 'as defined in Section 4' for Definition 3.1.1 (sourceIssues E3).

items.name: Theorem 4.1.4 (Scholze–Weinstein: p-divisible groups over O_C/p and bundles)
items.statement: (1) Every p-divisible group over O_C/p is quasi-isogenous to H ×_{F̄_p} O_C/p for some H over F̄_p; (2) G ↦ E(G) (the bundle of the graded module ⊕_d (M(G)[1/p])^{ϕ=p^d} on X_{C♭} = Proj ⊕ (B^+_cris)^{ϕ=p^d}) is fully faithful from p-divisible groups over O_C/p up to isogeny, with essential image the bundles with slopes in [0, 1]; (3) it agrees with E(D(G)[1/p]) by GAGA.
items.note: [SW13, Thm 5.1.4]; A_cris is the p-adic completion of the PD envelope of W(O_C♭) → O_C/p. The text says C has 'ring of integers O_C/p' (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: Scholze–Weinstein: classification of p-divisible groups over O_C
items.statement: p-divisible groups over O_C are equivalent to pairs (T, W) with T a finite free Z_p-module and W ⊂ T ⊗ C the Hodge–Tate filtration [SW13, Thm B]; the quasi-logarithm qlog : X̃^ad_η(R, R^+) → D(X)[1/p] ⊗ R identifies the image of T_pG ⊗ C with (Lie G^∨)^∨ ⊗ C [SW13, §3].
items.note: The input to Proposition 4.2.14, Lemma 4.2.18 and Lemma 4.3.20.

items.name: Lemmas 4.1.5–4.1.6 (Chai–Oort: the internal Hom p-divisible group)
items.statement: For isoclinic G, G' over a perfect field k, H_n = Hom(G[p^n], G'[p^n]); the images H_n^{(m)} of H_m stabilize to a finite group scheme H'_n; the maps ι_n (precompose p, include) send H'_n into H'_{n+1}, and H_{G,G'} = colim H'_n is a p-divisible group with H[p^n] = H'_n.
items.note: Construction of Chai and Oort, explained to the authors in 2014.

items.name: Lemmas 4.1.7–4.1.8 (Tate module and Dieudonné module of H_{G,G'})
items.statement: T_pH_{G,G'} = Hom(G, G'); D(H_{G,G'})[1/p] = Hom(D(G)[1/p], D(G')[1/p])^{≤0}, the slope ≤ 0 part of the internal Hom.
items.note: Proof via [SW13, Thm A] on f-semiperfect rings: no x ∈ A_cris(R) with p^aϕ^b(x) = x for a, b > 0. Chai–Oort prove it (integrally) by computing Frobenius.

items.name: Corollaries 4.1.10–4.1.11 (slopes of H_{G,G'})
items.statement: For isoclinic G, G': if slope G > slope G' then H_{G,G'} = 0; if equal, H is étale; if slope G < slope G', H is connected, and Hom(G, G') is represented by Spec k[[x_1^{1/p^∞}, …, x_r^{1/p^∞}]]/(x_1, …, x_r), r = dim H.

items.name: Unramified local PEL data and the p-divisible group X_b
items.statement: B semisimple over Q_p with anti-involution *, V a B-module with alternating (·,·), G(R) = {(g, c) : (gv, gw) = c(v, w)} connected (no type D); unramified: maximal *-stable order O_B and self-dual O_B-lattice Λ; µ with weights 0, 1 on V (V = V_0 ⊕ V_1, c∘µ = id); b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}); X_b over F̄_p with rational Dieudonné module (V ⊗ L, b(id ⊗ σ)), B-action and symmetric polarization; D = (B, *, V, (·,·), b, µ), D^int.
items.note: IG.0 plans the local deformation data for CSnc's split unitary datum.

items.name: Definition 4.2.1 and Theorem 4.2.2 (Rapoport–Zink spaces of PEL type)
items.statement: M_{D^int} on Nilp^op_{O_Ĕ}: pairs (G, ρ), G with O_B-action, principal polarization compatible with *, Kottwitz determinant condition [RZ96, 3.23], ρ : X_b ×_{F̄_p} R/p → G ×_R R/p a quasi-isogeny compatible with the extra structures up to a scalar; it is representable by a formally smooth formal scheme locally with finitely generated ideal of definition [RZ96, Thm 3.25, §3.82] (p = 2 allowed here).
items.note: Definition 4.2.1 writes O_{Ĕ_0} for O_Ĕ (sourceIssues E5).

items.name: Generic fibre, finite level and infinite level (Definition 4.2.3)
items.statement: M_{D^int} = (𝔐_{D^int})^ad_η in the sense of [SW13, §2]; M_{D^int,n} parametrizing O_B-linear Λ/p^n → G[p^n]^ad_η matching pairings via ζ_{p^n} (finite étale covers, [RZ96, L 5.33]); M_{D^int,∞}: triples (G, ρ, α) with α : Λ → T_pG^ad_η O_B-linear, matching pairings via (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p^2}, …) and an isomorphism at geometric points.

items.name: Theorem 4.2.4 (infinite-level RZ spaces of PEL type)
items.statement: M_{D^int,∞} is representable by a preperfectoid adic space over Spa(Ĕ(ζ_{p^∞}), O), M_{D^int,∞} ~ lim M_{D^int,n}, and it depends only on D: it is the sheafification of B-linear maps V → X̃_b^ad_η(R, R^+) matching pairings such that the image of V ⊗ R in D(X_b)[1/p] ⊗ R is totally isotropic, the quotient W is finite projective and locally V_1 ⊗ R, and 0 → V → X̃_b(C, C^+) → W ⊗ C → 0 is exact at geometric points.
items.note: After [SW13, §6] (EL case: Thm 6.5.4): a closed subfunctor of SW13's M_∞ (Grothendieck–Messing; [SW13, Prop. 3.3.3, Thm 6.3.4, Prop. 2.3.7, L 6.3.6]).

items.name: Propositions 4.2.5–4.2.6 (the local Hodge–Tate period map lands in the b-stratum)
items.statement: π_HT : M_{D,∞} → Fℓ_{G,µ} (V → X̃_b ↦ the quotient of V ⊗ R given by the image in D(X_b)[1/p] ⊗ R; Fℓ_{G,µ} = B-equivariant quotients W' with totally isotropic kernel, locally V_0 ⊗ R) is G(Q_p)-equivariant and factors through π^b_HT : M_{D,∞} → Fℓ^b_{G,µ}.
items.note: [SW13, Prop. 7.1.1]; the bundle E_V is the modification of V ⊗ O at ∞ by the lattice with Ξ/(V ⊗ B^+) = Lie G ⊗ C, equal to the bundle of G ×_{O_C} O_C/p by [SW13, Prop. 5.1.6]. The text refers to 'Theorem 3.5.9' for Corollary 3.5.9 (sourceIssues E6).

items.name: Remark 4.2.8 (local and global Hodge–Tate maps agree)
items.statement: For A/O_C and G = A[p^∞], the Hodge–Tate filtration on T_pG ⊗ C agrees with the one of §2 [Sch13d, Prop. 4.15], so local and global Hodge–Tate period maps are compatible.

items.name: Definition 4.2.9 and Lemma 4.2.10 (the automorphism group of X̃_b)
items.statement: Aut_G(X̃_b)(R) = {(α ∈ Aut_B(X̃_{b,R}), β ∈ Aut(µ̃_{p^∞,R})) : α respects the polarization up to β}, representable by a formal scheme over Spf W(F̄_p), locally Spf W(R) with R perfect.
items.note: Closed in products of H̃_{X_i,X_j} for a completely slope divisible X_b; IG.0 plans the automorphism group scheme for CSnc's datum.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.11 (structure of Aut_G(X̃_b))
items.statement: There is a natural map Aut_G(X̃_b) → J_b(Q_p) (J_b(Q_p) as a locally profinite formal scheme over W(F̄_p)) all of whose fibres are Spf W(F̄_p)[[x_1^{1/p^∞}, …, x_d^{1/p^∞}]] with d = ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩.
items.note: Reduction to EL and simple PEL data ([Ham15, §4.1, Cor. 4.5]): Res_{F/Q_p}GL_n, GSp_n/O_F and GU_n/O_{F^+} (the last left as an exercise); d_{i,j} = m_im_j(λ_j − λ_i) matches ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩ ([Ham15, App. A]). Remark 4.2.12: µ_{p^∞} × Q_p/Z_p; Remark 4.2.13: d is the dimension of central leaves [Ham15, Cor. 7.8].

items.name: Proposition 4.2.14 (fibres of the local period map are Aut_G(X̃_b)-torsors)
items.statement: The action map M̂_{D,∞} ×_{Spa(L,O_L)} Aut_G(X̃_b)^ad_η → (M_{D,∞} ×_{Fℓ_{G,µ}} M_{D,∞})^∧ is an isomorphism of perfectoid spaces.
items.note: Via Lemma 4.2.15 and [SW13, Thm B]; the target is not shown to be a torsor in any topology.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.15 (non-noetherian Berthelot: extending maps over R^+)
items.statement: Let R^+ be integrally closed in R = R^+[1/p] and G, H p-divisible groups over R^+ with constant Newton polygon on Spec R^+/p. A map f_R : G_R → H_R extends (uniquely) to R^+ if and only if it extends over O_C at every geometric rank-one point Spa(C, O_C).
items.note: Reduced to a valuation ring by the description R^+ = {f : |f(x)| ≤ 1 ∀x}.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.16 and Remark 4.2.17 (homomorphisms over valuation rings of characteristic p)
items.statement: For V a valuation ring of characteristic p with fraction field K and G, H p-divisible over V with constant Newton polygon, Hom(G, H) → Hom(G_K, H_K) is bijective; consequently Berthelot's full faithfulness [Ber80] holds over any integral domain.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.18 (surjectivity onto the b-stratum)
items.statement: For C/Ĕ(ζ_{p^∞}) algebraically closed, π^b_HT : M_{D,∞}(C, O_C) → Fℓ^b_{G,µ}(C, O_C) is surjective.
items.note: [SW13, Thm B] and Theorem 4.1.4.

items.name: Propositions 4.2.19–4.2.21 (dimension of partially proper adic spaces)
items.statement: For X partially proper over Spa(K, O_K) (Remark 4.2.20: X(K, K^+) → X(K, O_K) ×_{Y(K,O_K)} Y(K, K^+) bijective), dim X (Krull dimension of |X|) is the maximal transcendence degree over k of the residue fields k(x) of O_{K(x)}; for f : X → Y of such spaces and a rank-one x ↦ y, dim cl_X{x} = dim cl_Y{y} + dim cl_{X_y}{x}.
items.note: Closures of rank-one points are Zariski–Riemann spaces of k(x)/k. Partial properness itself is planned by H3.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.22 (dimension of the automorphism group)
items.statement: For K complete over Ĕ, Aut_G(X̃_b)^ad ×_{Spa(O_Ĕ)} Spa(K, O_K) is partially proper over Spa(K, O_K) of dimension ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩.
items.note: Components Spa(O_Ĕ[[x_i^{1/p^∞}]]); after tilting a d-dimensional open unit disc.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.23 (dimension of the Newton strata of the flag variety)
items.statement: dim Fℓ^b_{G,µ} = ⟨2ρ, µ⟩ − ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩.
items.note: Fℓ_{G,µ} and M_{D,∞} are partially proper of dimension ⟨2ρ, µ⟩; Lemma 4.2.18, Propositions 4.2.14, 4.2.21–4.2.22. The converse inequality picks 'y ∈ Fℓ_{G,µ}' where y ∈ Fℓ^b_{G,µ} is needed (sourceIssues E7).

items.name: Global unramified PEL data and their moduli spaces
items.statement: B simple over Q with center F, V faithful, positive involution *, alternating (·,·), G(R) = {x ∈ End_B(V ⊗ R) : xx* ∈ R^×} connected, h with (v, h(i)w) positive definite; unramified at p (O_B, self-dual Λ, G_{Z_(p)}, K_p = G_{Z_(p)}(Z_p) hyperspecial); the moduli space S_{K^pK_p} over O_{E,p} [Kot92b], whose generic fibre is |ker^1(Q, G)| copies of the Shimura variety.
items.note: PELModuli M1–M2 own the PEL functor, representability and smoothness at good level.

items.name: The Newton stratification of the special fibre
items.statement: A point of S_{K^pK_p} ×_{O_{E,p}} F_q gives a p-divisible group with extra structure, hence b ∈ B(G), which lies in B(G, µ^{-1}) [RR96]; strata S^b_{K^pK_p} are locally closed.
items.note: IG.0 builds the Newton map into B(G_{Q_p}, µ^{-1}) for its PEL datum.

items.name: Definition 4.3.1 and Proposition 4.3.3 (the perfect Igusa variety Ig^b)
items.statement: Ig^b over F̄_q: pairs (A, ρ), A ∈ S_{K^pK_p}(R) with extra structures and ρ : A[p^∞] ≅ X_b ×_{F̄_p} R compatible with them (the polarization up to a scalar); representable by a scheme (an inverse limit of isomorphism schemes over S_{K^pK_p} ⊗ F̄_q).
items.note: IG.1 constructs Ig^X for CSnc's datum; this is the general PEL form, which differs from Mantovan's definition.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.4 and Corollary 4.3.5 (Aut_G(X̃_b) acts; Ig^b is perfect)
items.statement: Ig^b(R) = {(A, ρ̃): A up to p-power isogeny, ρ̃ : A[p^∞] → X_b × R a quasi-isogeny}; hence the formal group Aut_G(X̃_b) acts on Ig^b, and Frobenius is an automorphism of Ig^b.
items.note: Frobenius pullback is an equivalence up to p-power isogeny (Verschiebung).

items.name: Central leaves and Mantovan's Igusa varieties (Definition 4.3.6)
items.statement: The leaf C^b = {x ∈ S^b : A_x[p^∞] ≅ X_b geometrically}, closed in S^b and smooth with its reduced structure [Man05, Prop. 1]; G_b = A[p^∞]|C^b is completely slope divisible with graded pieces G^i_b of slopes λ_i; I^b_Mant → C^b parametrizes isomorphisms ρ_i : G^i_b ≅ X_i compatible with O_B and the polarizations; I^b_{Mant,m} trivializes p^m-torsion liftably and is a torsor under an étale group scheme (Remark 4.3.7, [Man05, Prop. 4]); I^b_Mant = lim_m I^b_{Mant,m} is a pro-étale cover of C^b.
items.note: C^b depends on X_b within its isogeny class.

items.name: Proposition 1.12 = Proposition 4.3.8 (Ig^b is the perfection of Mantovan's Igusa variety)
items.statement: The natural map Ig^b → I^b_Mant identifies Ig^b with the perfection of I^b_Mant; in particular their étale cohomology agrees, and the J_b(Q_p)-action on the cohomology of Ig^b recovers Mantovan's.
items.note: Canonical splitting of the slope filtration over the perfection using F^s/p^{t_i}, λ_i = t_i/s. Only a submonoid of J_b(Q_p) acts on I^b_Mant.

items.name: Corollary 4.3.9 (Ig^b → C^b is faithfully flat)
items.statement: Ig^b → C^b is faithfully flat, hence a torsor under the (nonreduced) automorphism group of X_b; this forces dim C^b = ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩.

items.name: Lemmas 4.3.10 and 4.3.12 (the deformation 𝔛^b = Ig^b × M^b)
items.statement: Ig^b lifts uniquely to a flat formal scheme Ig^b_{O_Ĕ}; for a lift (X_b)_{O_K} ∈ M^b(O_K), Ig^b_{O_K}(R) = {(A, ρ : A[p^∞] ≅ (X_b)_{O_K} × R)}. With 𝔛^b (Definition 4.3.11: (A, ρ), ρ a quasi-isogeny A[p^∞] × R/p → X_b × R/p), Ig^b_{O_K} ×_{O_Ĕ} M^b ≅ 𝔛^b_{O_K} over M^b; 𝔛^b is a formal scheme.
items.note: 𝔛^b should be an Aut_G(X̃_b)-torsor over the completion of S_{K^pK_p} along S^b; only the quasitorsor property is proved.

items.name: Proposition 1.13 = Proposition 4.3.13 (the J_b(Q_p)-torsor over a Newton stratum)
items.statement: For S over F̄_p and X a p-divisible group with extra structure all of whose fibres are quasi-isogenous to X_b, the quasi-isogenies between X_x̄ and X_b form a J_b(Q_p)-torsor on S_proét [BS15]; for S connected and locally topologically noetherian this is π_1^proét(S, x̄) → J_b(Q_p) (Remark 4.3.14), with compact image if X has a slope filtration and discrete cocompact image on the basic stratum.
items.locator: §1, Proposition 1.13, Remark 1.14, p. 656; §4.3, Proposition 4.3.13, Remark 4.3.14, pp. 720–724
items.note: Uses [OZ02, Ex. 4.2] for the non-slope-filtration phenomenon and [Sch13a, L 4.4] for the finite-level torsor; not used later.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.15 and Remark 4.3.16 (constant Newton polygon over strictly henselian perfect rings)
items.statement: For R strictly henselian perfect with residue field k, reduction to k is an equivalence between p-divisible groups over R with constant Newton polygon up to isogeny and p-divisible groups over k up to isogeny; p^cψ_k lifts for a constant c depending only on the heights.
items.note: Dieudonné full faithfulness over perfect rings (Gabber, [Ber80], [Lau13, Thm D]); minimal primes and the v-cover R → R̃ [BS17, Thm 4.1(i)]; cf. [OZ02, Cor. 3.4, 3.6].

items.name: Definition 4.3.17, Remark 4.3.18 and Corollary 4.3.19 (the infinite-level space X^b_∞)
items.statement: X^b_∞ over (Ĕ(ζ_{p^∞}), O): (A, ρ, α) with α : Λ → T_pA trivializing compatibly; X^b_∞ = X^b ×_{M^b} M^b_∞ is an adic space, and (Ig^b_{O_K})^ad_η ×_{Spa(Ĕ,O_Ĕ)} M^b_∞ ≅ X^b_{∞,K}, so X^b_∞ is preperfectoid.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.20 (the product formula)
items.statement: With S^b_{K^p} ⊂ S_{K^p} the locally closed preimage of S^b under specialization, X̂^b_∞ → (M^b_∞ ×_{Fℓ_{G,µ}} S^b_{K^p})^∧ is an isomorphism of perfectoid spaces: X^b_∞ → M^b_∞, X^b_∞ → S^b_{K^p} over π^b_HT and π_HT is Cartesian on perfectoid points.
items.note: [SW13, Thm B] on (C, O_C)-points, Lemma 4.2.15 in general.

items.name: Lemma 4.4.1 (stalks of pushforwards are cohomology of fibres)
items.statement: For f : Y → X qcqs, X locally strongly noetherian or perfectoid, Y perfectoid, and a geometric point x̄ = Spa(C(x̄), C(x̄)^+) → X, (R^if_*G)_x̄ ≅ H^i(Y_x̄, G) with Y_x̄ = (Y ×_X Spa(C(x̄), C(x̄)^+))^∧.
items.note: [SW13, Prop. 2.4.3], [Sch12, Cor. 7.18] (footnotes 24–25).

items.name: Lemma 4.4.2 (cohomology is determined by rank-one points)
items.statement: For X qcqs perfectoid and U ⊂ X a quasicompact open containing all rank-one points, H^i(X, G) ≅ H^i(U, G) for locally constant G.
items.note: Footnote 26: also for strongly noetherian adic spaces.

items.name: Lemma 4.4.3 (perfect schemes and their canonical lifts)
items.statement: For X/F̄_p perfect and C algebraically closed with residue field ⊃ F̄_p, X_{O_C} the flat lift of X × O_C/p and X_C its perfectoid generic fibre, H^i(X, Z/ℓ^n) ← H^i(X_{O_C}, Z/ℓ^n) → H^i(X_C, Z/ℓ^n) are isomorphisms.
items.note: Reduce to the perfection of a finite-type X_0; tilting; [Hub96, Cor. 3.5.17], [DK73, XIII 2.1.4] and universal local acyclicity [Del77, Th. finitude 2.13].

items.name: Theorem 1.15 = Theorem 4.4.4 (fibres of π_HT are Igusa varieties)
items.statement: For compact PEL Shimura varieties of type (A) or (C) with good reduction at p (S_{K^pK_p} proper over O_{E,p}), ℓ ≠ p and a geometric point x̄ of Fℓ_{G,µ} in Fℓ^b_{G,µ}: (R^iπ_HT* Z/ℓ^n)_x̄ ≅ H^i(Ig^b, Z/ℓ^n) = lim_m H^i(I^b_{Mant,m}, Z/ℓ^n), depending only on a lift of x̄ to M^b_∞ and compatible with the G(A^p_f)-Hecke action.
items.note: Lemmas 4.4.1–4.4.3, 4.2.18, 4.3.20, Corollary 4.3.19, Proposition 4.3.8; properness is equivalent to G anisotropic [Lan11]. IG.3 plans the compactified non-compact version (CSnc Thm 4.1.1).

items.name: The unitary setup of §5.1
items.statement: F = F^+·K with F^+ totally real and K imaginary quadratic, G/Q a unitary similitude group of an alternating hermitian form on V (dim_F V = n) with (1) F^+ ≠ Q, (2) primes ramified in F lie in Spl_{F/F^+}, (3) G quasi-split at all finite places; h : C → End_F(V)_R giving a PEL datum of type (A); p unramified in F and split in K; G_{Q_p} = ∏_i Res_{F_{p_i}/Q_p} GL_n × G_m, J_b = ∏ J_{b_i} × G_m.
items.note: Footnote 27: (2) implies (1). CSnc (and IG) treat the quasi-split non-compact datum instead.

items.name: Endoscopic data, transfer factors and the fundamental lemma
items.statement: Endoscopic triples (H, s, η) [Kot84, 7.4], elliptic ones E_ell(G), extensions η̃ : ^LH → ^LG [Lan79]; Langlands–Shelstad transfer factors Δ [LS87]; the fundamental lemma and transfer (Ngô, Waldspurger): SO_{γ_H}(φ^H) = Σ_γ Δ(γ_H, γ)e(G_γ)O_γ(φ), with φ^H = η̃^*(φ) for unramified data.
items.note: ET.0 (endoscopic data), ET.1 (transfer factors), ET.3 (fundamental lemma and transfer). The text defines ellipticity by (Z(Ĥ)^Γ)° ⊂ Z(G) for Z(Ĝ) (sourceIssues E8).

items.name: Acceptable functions and Shin's test functions (Definition 5.2.2)
items.statement: φ ∈ C^∞_c(G(A^p_f) × J_b(Q_p)) is acceptable [Shi09, Defs 6.1–6.2] when φ_p is supported on ν_b-acceptable δ (v_p(e_i) < v_p(e_j) whenever λ_i > λ_j), and a high Frobenius twist of any φ is acceptable [Shi09, L 6.3]; φ^H = φ^{H,p}φ^H_pφ^H_∞ with Langlands–Shelstad transfer away from p, Kottwitz's φ^H_∞ [Kot90, §7] and Shin's φ^H_p [Shi10, §6].
items.note: ET.5 constructs acceptable functions and the matching p-test function.

items.name: Theorem 5.2.3 (Shin: stable trace formula for Igusa varieties)
items.statement: For acceptable φ, tr(φ | ι_ℓH_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)) = |ker^1(Q, G)| Σ_{(H,s,η)∈E_ell(G)} ι(G, H) ST^H_e(φ^H), ι(G, H) = τ(G)τ(H)^{-1}|Out(H, s, η)|^{-1}; valid for PEL data of type (A) or (C) (Remark 5.2.4).
items.note: [Shi10, Thm 7.2]; ET.5 proves the stable Igusa identity with the ker^1 and ι(G, H) factors.

items.name: Corollary 5.2.5 and Remark 5.2.6 (Shin's formula for the unitary group)
items.statement: With E_ell(G_n) represented by (G_n, 1, id) and (G_{n_1,n_2}, (1, (I_{n_1}, −I_{n_2})), η_{n_1,n_2}), n_1 + n_2 = n, n_1 ≥ n_2 (G_n⃗(R) = {(λ, g) : gΦ_n⃗ ᵗg^c = λΦ_n⃗}, (Φ_n)_{ij} = (−1)^{i+1}δ_{i,n+1−j}), extended by a Hecke character ϖ of A_K^×/K^× restricting to the quadratic character of K/Q: tr(φ | ι_ℓH_c(I^b_Mant)) = |ker^1(Q, G)| Σ_n⃗ ι(G, G_n⃗) ST^{G_n⃗}_e(φ^n⃗), ι = ½τ(G)τ(G_n⃗)^{-1} for n⃗ = (n/2, n/2) and τ(G)τ(G_n⃗)^{-1} otherwise.
items.note: [Shi11, §§3.1–3.5, Prop. 7.1]; the infinity functions φ^n⃗_∞ are combinations of Euler–Poincaré functions for the inner form G over R of arbitrary signature ([Shi11, 5.11]).

items.name: Base change, the twisted group and Lefschetz functions
items.statement: 𝒢_n⃗ = Res_{K/Q}(G_n⃗ ×_Q K), the L-morphisms BC_n⃗ and ζ̃ with the commutative diagram (5.3.1), BC-transfer of functions ([Shi11, §4]; surjective at split places), 𝒢^+_n⃗ = (Res_{K/Q}GL_1 × Res_{F/Q}GL_n⃗) ⋊ {1, θ}, Labesse's twisted Lefschetz functions f_{𝒢_n⃗,Ξ} [Lab91] matching Euler–Poincaré functions, and the invariant twisted trace formula I_geom(fθ) = I_spec(fθ) ([Art88a], [Art88b]).
items.note: ET.4 constructs the cyclic twisted trace identity, BC transfers and infinity pseudocoefficients for CSnc's G_n⃗. The text names the Hecke character ψ (sourceIssues E9).

items.name: Proposition 5.3.1 (Shin: geometric side as stable orbital integrals)
items.statement: For BC-matching φ = φ^Sφ_{S_fin}φ_{G_n⃗,ξ} and f = f^Sf_{S_fin}f_{𝒢_n⃗,Ξ}, I^{𝒢_n⃗θ}_geom(fθ) = τ(G_n⃗)^{-1} ST^{G_n⃗}_e(φ).
items.note: [Shi11, Cor. 4.7]; [Lab99, Thm 4.3.4], cuspidality of the Lefschetz function and [F^+ : Q] ≥ 2. ET.4 proves this equality.

items.name: Theorem 5.3.2 (the Igusa trace as twisted spectral sides)
items.statement: tr(φ | ι_ℓ[H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]) = |ker^1(Q, G)|τ(G) Σ_{G_n⃗} ε_n⃗ I^{𝒢_n⃗θ}_spec(f^n⃗θ), ε_n⃗ = ½ for n⃗ = (n/2, n/2) and 1 otherwise, for the test functions built from (f^n)^S, f^n_{S_fin∖{p}} and an acceptable φ_p as in [Shi11, proof of Thm 6.1].
items.note: Corollary 5.2.5, Remark 5.2.6, Proposition 5.3.1 and (5.3.2); q(G) = ½dim(G(R)/K_∞A°_∞) for an inner form of arbitrary signature.

items.name: Proposition 5.3.3 (Shin: the twisted spectral side)
items.statement: I^{𝒢_n⃗θ}_spec(f^n⃗θ) = Σ_M |W_M||W_G|^{-1} |det(Φ_n⃗^{-1}θ − 1)_{a^{𝒢θ}_M}|^{-1} Σ_{Π_M} tr(n-Ind^{𝒢_n⃗}_Q(Π_M)_ξ(f^n⃗) ∘ A'), Π_M running over Φ_n⃗^{-1}θ-stable subrepresentations of R_{M,disc}.

items.name: Decent elements and J_b as an inner form of the Levi M_b
items.statement: b admits a decent representative b̃ ((b̃σ)^s = sν_b̃(p)σ^s, [RZ96, Def. 1.8], [Kot85, §4.3]) with ν defined over Q_p (G quasi-split); M_b = Cent_G(ν) is a Q_p-rational Levi, b is basic in M_b and J_b is an inner form of M_b.
items.note: BG0 constructs J_b as the σ-centralizer with its inner-Levi description.

items.name: Shin's transfer at p and the map Red^b_n⃗
items.statement: E^eff_p(J_b, G, G_n⃗) [Shi09, §6.2]; φ^n⃗_p is obtained by transfer from J_b(Q_p) to M_{G_n⃗}(Q_p) and then to G_n⃗(Q_p) (using acceptability, [Shi10, L 3.9]); dually Red^b_n⃗ : Groth(G_n⃗(Q_p)) → Groth(J_b(Q_p)) is normalized Jacquet functors, transfer along η̃_n⃗ (normalized parabolic induction) and the Langlands–Jacquet map [Bad07] ([Shi11, §5.5]; Remark 5.4.1 for n⃗ = (n)).
items.note: ET.5 (the p-test function), ET.6 (inner forms of GL_m), ET.7b (Jacquet functors and inner-form transfer for the Igusa trace).

items.name: Lemma 5.4.2 (Red^b_n⃗ is dual to φ ↦ φ^n⃗_p)
items.statement: For π_p ∈ Groth(G_n⃗(Q_p)), tr π_p(φ^n⃗_p) = tr(Red^b_n⃗(π_p))(φ_p).

items.name: Lemma 5.4.3 (generic principal series die under Red^b)
items.statement: If π^n⃗_p = ⊗π^n⃗_{p_i} ⊗ π^n⃗_0 has some π^n⃗_{p_i} transferring to a generic principal series of GL_n(F_{p_i}) while J_{b_i} is a non-quasi-split inner form of M_{b_i}, then Red^b_n⃗(π_p) = 0.
items.note: Generic principal series components lie in the kernel of the Langlands–Jacquet map for non-quasi-split inner forms ([Bad07, Thm 3.1, Prop. 3.3]); the L-morphism ^LM_{G_n⃗} → ^LM_b restricts η̃_{n_1,n_2} [Shi10, §2].

items.name: Lemma 5.5.1 (the Igusa trace through θ-stable automorphic representations)
items.statement: tr(φ | ι_ℓ[H_c(I^b_Mant)]) is a linear combination of tr((Π^n⃗)^S((f^n⃗)^S) ∘ A^S) · tr((Π^n⃗)_{S_fin∖{p}}(…)) · tr(Red^b_n⃗(π^n⃗_p)(φ_p)), where π^n⃗_p base changes to Π^n⃗_p, Π^n⃗ = (n-Ind^{𝒢_n⃗}_Q Π_M)_ξ is a θ-stable isobaric irreducible automorphic representation of 𝒢_n⃗ with Π_M in the (relatively) discrete spectrum of a Levi M and Π^n⃗_∞ cohomological for the trivial representation; this holds for every φ_p, not only acceptable ones.
items.note: After [Shi11, Prop. 6.1]: Theorem 5.3.2, Proposition 5.3.3, Moeglin–Waldspurger [MW89], Jacquet–Shalika [JS81], injectivity of base change at split p, Lemma 5.4.2 and [Shi09, proof of L 6.4] to remove acceptability.

items.name: Corollary 5.5.2 and Remark 5.5.3 (Hecke eigensystems occurring in Igusa cohomology)
items.statement: If Π^n⃗ contributes, the transfer of (Π^n⃗)^S to 𝒢_n via ζ̃_n⃗,* occurs in BC^S([H_c(I^b_Mant)]^{S-ur}); conversely every irreducible G(A^S)-subrepresentation of BC^S([H_c(I^b_Mant)]^{S-ur}) is Π^S with Π = ζ̃_n⃗*(Π^n⃗), possibly for several n⃗.
items.note: Linear independence of unramified Hecke characters; Case ST of [Shi11, §6].

items.name: L-algebraic and C-algebraic automorphic representations
items.statement: The notions of [BG14]; for GL_m they differ by a twist, and Π_i|det|^{(1−n_i)/2} is regular L-algebraic when Π_i is regular C-algebraic.
items.note: AG2.0 defines regular algebraic representations and the normalizations.

items.name: Galois representations of regular algebraic conjugate self-dual cuspidal representations
items.statement: For Π regular L-algebraic, conjugate self-dual and cuspidal on GL_m(A_F) there is r_Π : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_m(Q̄_ℓ) with WD(r_Π|_{G_{F_q}})^{F-ss} ≅ ι_ℓ^{-1}rec(Π_q) at every place ([Shi11], [CH13], [Car12]); for the simple Shimura varieties of §5.6 via Shin's stable base change (appendix to [Gol14]).
items.note: AG2.2 (polarized cuspidal systems) and AG2.5 (local–global comparison). Footnote 28: compatibility up to semisimplification suffices.

items.name: Theorem 5.5.4 (Galois representations for the pieces Π_i)
items.statement: Writing Π^n⃗ = ψ ⊗ Π_1 ⊗ Π_2 on 𝒢_{n_1,n_2}(A) = A_K^× × GL_{n_1}(A_F) × GL_{n_2}(A_F), there is r_i : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_{n_i}(Q̄_ℓ) with WD(r_i|Gal(F̄_q/F_q))^{F-ss} ≅ ι_ℓ^{-1}rec(Π_{i,q}|det|^{(1−n_i)/2}) for every place q of F ([HT01] normalization).
items.note: Π_i = n-Ind(Π_{M_i}) with Π_{M_i} built from regular L-algebraic conjugate self-dual cuspidal representations [MW89]. The statement prints GL_n for GL_{n_i}, and the decomposition writes A^×_{F_0} for A^×_K (sourceIssues E10, E11).

items.name: Corollary 5.5.5 (Galois representations for Igusa Hecke eigensystems)
items.statement: For an irreducible Π^S ⊂ BC^S([H_c(I^b_Mant)]^{S-ur}) there is r_{Π^S,ℓ} : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(Q̄_ℓ), unramified outside S ∪ {ℓ}, such that at places v of F above q ∈ Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}) the characteristic polynomial of Frob_v is the image of X^n − T_{1,v}X^{n−1} + … + (−1)^iq_v^{i(i−1)/2}T_{i,v}X^{n−i} + … + (−1)^nq_v^{n(n−1)/2}T_{n,v} under the Satake parameters of Π^S and ι_ℓ^{-1}.
items.note: r_{Π^S,ℓ} = ⊕ r_i ⊗ ε_i, ε_i attached to |det|^{(n_i−n)/2}ϖ(N_{F/K}∘det)^{ε(n−n_i)}, ϖ_∞(z) = (z/z̄)^{δ/2} with δ odd. T_{i,v} is printed inside 𝔾(Q_q) = ∏ GL_n(F_w) × Q_p^× × Q_p^× with Q_q meant, and Spl_{F_0/Q} for Spl_{K/Q} (sourceIssues E11, E12).

items.name: Remark 5.5.6 (local–global compatibility at p)
items.statement: For Π = ζ̃_n⃗,*(Π^n⃗) and p = ∏ p_i in F, Π_{p_i} and r_{Π^S,ℓ}|Gal(F̄_{p_i}/F_{p_i}) correspond under the geometric local Langlands correspondence; if the latter is ⊕ χ_{i,a} with χ_{i,a}χ_{i,b}^{-1} never cyclotomic, Π_{p_i} is a generic principal series.
items.note: From the local–global compatibility in Theorem 5.5.4.

items.name: Theorem 5.5.7 (genericity forces the µ-ordinary stratum)
items.statement: Let S_i = {τ : F ↪ C | ι_p∘τ induces p_i}. Assume each S_i contains at most one τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0 (signature (p_τ, q_τ)), and for each such i r|Gal(F̄_{p_i}/F_{p_i}) = ⊕ χ_{i,a} with χ_{i,a}χ_{i,b}^{-1} not cyclotomic for a ≠ b. Then BC^p([H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]^{S-ur})_r = 0 for every b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}) that is not µ-ordinary.
items.note: Lemmas 5.4.3, 5.5.1, 5.5.8; B(G, µ^{-1}) = ∏ B(G_i, µ_i^{-1}) (footnote 30: B(H/L) = B(L, H)); footnote 29: 'µ^{-1}-ordinary'.

items.name: Lemma 5.5.8 (only the µ-ordinary class has quasi-split J_b)
items.statement: For L p-adic and µ : t ↦ diag(t, …, t, 1, …, 1) (n − q entries t), exactly one b ∈ B(GL_n/L, µ^{-1}) has J_b quasi-split: the µ-ordinary element diag(ϖ^{-1}, …, ϖ^{-1}, 1, …, 1) (n − q entries ϖ^{-1}), with J_b ≅ GL_{n−q} × GL_q.
items.note: A nonintegral slope λ gives a factor GL over the division algebra of invariant λ mod 1; κ(b) = −µ.

items.name: Proposition 5.6.1 (Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties: no endoscopy)
items.statement: For a PEL datum (B, *, V, ⟨,⟩, h) with B a division algebra over F, V simple and * of the second kind (proper, no endoscopy), B split above p, and φ = φ^pφ_p with φ_p acceptable: tr(φ | ι_ℓH_c(I^b_Mant)) = |ker^1(Q, G)|ι(G, G_n)ST^{G_n}_e(φ^{G_n}), G_n the quasi-split inner form.
items.note: The other terms vanish by [Shi10, L 7.1]; following [Shi12, §6] without assuming p inert in F^+.

items.name: Corollary 5.6.2 (Igusa cohomology of simple Shimura varieties)
items.statement: Combining with the stable trace formula for S_K ([Art89, Thm 6.1], [Shi12, Prop. 6.3]) and Matsushima's formula: Red^b_n([H(S_K, Q̄_ℓ)]) = ε_G d(G_R) [H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)] and [ι_ℓH_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)] = (−1)^{q(G)} Σ_{π_f} c(π_f)[π_f^p][Red^b_n(π_p)] in Groth(G(A^p_f) × J_b(Q_p)), over π_f with π_fπ_∞ automorphic for some π_∞ cohomological for the trivial representation.
items.note: Analogue of [Shi12, Cor. 6.12]; [Shi11, L 6.4] extends to all φ_p; ε_G, d(G_R) nonzero constants and c(π_f) related to automorphic multiplicities.

items.name: Corollary 5.6.3 (Theorem 5.5.7 for simple Shimura varieties)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 5.5.7 on S_i and r, [H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]_r = 0 for every b ∈ B(G, µ^{-1}) that is not µ-ordinary.
items.note: Same proof as Theorem 5.5.7; includes Shimura varieties with q-adic uniformization (level raising [Tho14]).

items.name: Theorem 6.1.1 (Illusie: nearby cycles preserve perversity)
items.statement: For K complete discretely valued, ℓ invertible in O_K, X of finite type over O_K and F a perverse F_ℓ-sheaf on X_η, RψF = i^*Rj_*F|_{X_η̄} is perverse on X_s̄ [Ill94, Cor. 4.5].
items.note: LPV.6 (perverse nearby cycles).

items.name: Theorem 6.1.2 (Huber: algebraic and formal nearby cycles agree)
items.statement: With λ : X_η̄,ét → (X_s̄)_ét lifting étale maps to formal schemes over O_C, Rλ_*(F^ad|X_η̄) ≅ RψF [Hub96, Thm 3.5.13].
items.note: H1:formal-adic-comparison plans Hub96 3.5.13 with its hypotheses.

items.name: Equivariant sites and nearby cycles of K_p-equivariant formal models
items.statement: The equivariant sites (Fℓ_{G,µ}/G(Q_p))_ét and (S_{K^p}/G(Q_p))_ét of Scholze's Lubin–Tate tower paper, §2, with slice categories, passage to limits and continuity of K_p-actions on affinoid étale U = Spa(A, A°) (its Cor. 2.5, Props 2.8, 2.9, 2.12); for small K_p acting trivially on 𝔘_s, λ_{U/K_p} : (U_η̄/K_p)_ét → 𝔘_s̄,ét.
items.note: Cited as [Sch15b], whose bibliography entry duplicates [Sch15a] (sourceIssues E13); arXiv v1 cites the Lubin–Tate tower paper here.

items.name: Proposition 6.1.3 (nearby cycles of Rπ_HT* F_ℓ are perverse)
items.statement: For π_HT : S_{K^p} → Fℓ_{G,µ} of a compact Hodge-type Shimura variety and small K^p, every geometric point x̄ has a basis of affinoid étale neighbourhoods U = Spa(A, A°), 𝔘 = Spf A°, such that Rλ_{U/K_p*}(R(π_HT/G(Q_p))_*F_ℓ)|_{U_η̄/K_p}[⟨2ρ, µ⟩] is perverse on 𝔘_s̄ for every small pro-p K_p ⊂ G(Q_p).
items.note: π_HT is partially proper; mod p the map factors through a finite-type map satisfying the valuative criterion, hence finite (footnote 32: π_HT,U_s is ind-finite though π_HT,U has positive-dimensional fibres); Theorems 6.1.1–6.1.2. IG.4 plans the non-compact semiperversity (CSnc Thm 4.6.1).

items.name: Corollary 6.1.4 (concentration for Igusa varieties at a minimal stratum)
items.statement: Let T^S = Z[G(A^S_f)//K_S] and m ⊂ T^S maximal. Among b with H^i(Ig^b, F_ℓ)[m] ≠ 0 for some i take one with d = ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩ minimal; then H^i(Ig^b, F_ℓ)[m] ≠ 0 only for i = d.
items.note: Averaging over compact opens of J_b(Q_p) makes m-torsion and localization equivalent; (Rπ_HT*F_ℓ)_m is supported on Fℓ^{≥d}; dimension ⟨2ρ, µ⟩ − d (Proposition 4.2.23); a perverse sheaf is concentrated in one degree on its largest stratum.

items.name: Lemma 6.2.2 (decomposed generic reductions)
items.statement: If ρ : Gal(L̄/L) → GL_n(Q̄_ℓ) has decomposed generic reduction, then ρ = ⊕ χ_i with χ_a/χ_b not cyclotomic for a ≠ b; the corresponding representation of GL_n(L) is a generic principal series.
items.note: Obstructions H^1(Gal(L̄/L), χ̄_a/χ̄_b) vanish since H^1 of the unramified character χ_λ is 0 for λ ∉ {1, q}.

items.name: The compact unitary Shimura varieties of §6.3 and the Hecke algebra T^S
items.statement: Case 1: B a central division algebra over F with V ≅ B; Case 2: B = F, F^+ ≠ Q, G quasi-split at all finite places and F/F^+ split above primes ramified in F; S finite outside which F and G are unramified (S ⊂ Spl_{F/F^+} in Case 2); T^S = ⊗_{q∈Spl_{K/Q}∖(S∪{ℓ})} Z[G(Q_q)//K_q].

items.name: Theorem 6.3.1(1) (Galois representations for torsion Hecke eigensystems)
items.statement: For a maximal ideal m ⊂ T^S with H^i(S_K, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0 for some i there is a unique semisimple continuous ρ_m : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(F̄_ℓ) unramified outside S ∪ {ℓ} with the characteristic polynomial of ρ_m(Frob_v), v above q ∈ Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}), the image of X^n − T_{1,v}X^{n−1} ± … + (−1)^iq_v^{i(i−1)/2}T_{i,v}X^{n−i} + … under T^S/m ↪ F̄_ℓ.
items.note: Hochschild–Serre to infinite level at a split p, Leray for π_HT, Corollary 6.1.4, concentration and flatness in the middle degree, Poincaré duality and Corollary 5.5.5. T_{i,v} is again printed inside a G(Q_q) with factor Q_p^× (sourceIssues E12).

items.name: Theorem 6.3.1(2) (middle-degree concentration)
items.statement: Suppose some p ∈ Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}), p = uu^c, and a prime 𝔭 | p of E are such that for the primes p_i | u of F each S_i contains at most one τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0, and ρ_m is decomposed generic at p_i whenever it does. Then H^i(S_K, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0 only for i = dim S_K.
items.note: The minimal b is µ-ordinary by Theorem 5.5.7 and Lemma 6.2.2, and then ⟨2ρ, µ⟩ = ⟨2ρ, ν_b⟩ = dim S_K; Leray for π_HT gives vanishing below the middle, Poincaré duality (dual ideal) above.

items.name: Remarks 6.3.2–6.3.3 (how to satisfy condition (2))

routes.title: Igusa varieties, compactified period fibers and torsion concentration, Part II: compact unitary Shimura varieties
routes.brief:
Starts where Igusa varieties, compactified period fibers and torsion concentration (IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration) stops. That roadmap proves torsion concentration for the non-compact quasi-split unitary datum of Caraiani–Scholze's sequel (CSnc), and restricts its geometry to that datum. This Part II proves the compact theorem of Caraiani–Scholze, 'On the generic part of the cohomology of compact unitary Shimura varieties' (Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), 649–766; CS17): arbitrary signature, Kottwitz's simple Shimura varieties and compact unitary groups quasi-split at all finite places, with endoscopy. Its first prerequisite is IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration; this paper's source route extends IG.0–IG.4 to general compact PEL data of type (A)/(C), and this Part II imports them.

Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 6.3.1: let S_K be a compact PEL Shimura variety of type A for F = F^+·K (Case 1: B a central division algebra over F, V ≅ B; Case 2: B = F, F^+ ≠ Q, G quasi-split at all finite places, F/F^+ split above primes ramified in F), S a finite set of primes with K = K_SK^S, K^S hyperspecial (S ⊂ Spl_{F/F^+} in Case 2), T^S = ⊗_{q∈Spl_{K/Q}∖(S∪{ℓ})} Z[G(Q_q)//K_q], and m ⊂ T^S maximal with H^i(S_K, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0 for some i. (1) There is a unique semisimple continuous ρ_m : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(F̄_ℓ), unramified outside S ∪ {ℓ}, with the characteristic polynomial of ρ_m(Frob_v), v above q ∈ Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}), the image of X^n − T_{1,v}X^{n−1} ± … + (−1)^iq_v^{i(i−1)/2}T_{i,v}X^{n−i} + … + (−1)^nq_v^{n(n−1)/2}T_{n,v}. (2) If some p ∈ Spl_{K/Q} ∖ (S ∪ {ℓ}), p = uu^c, and 𝔭 | p in E are such that for each prime p_i | u of F the set S_i = {τ : ι_p∘τ induces p_i} contains at most one τ with p_τq_τ ≠ 0, and ρ_m is decomposed generic at p_i whenever it does, then H^i(S_K, F_ℓ)_m ≠ 0 only for i = dim S_K. Theorem 1.1 is the case of a p completely decomposed in F (Remark 6.3.2); Remark 6.3.3 treats signature (0, n) at all but one place; Remarks 1.3 and 1.7.1 give torsion-freeness of the localized Z_ℓ-cohomology and twisted coefficients. Decomposed generic (Definition 1.9 = 6.2.1): unramified with Frobenius eigenvalue ratios outside {1, q}.

Layers. (1) The unitary setup of §5.1 and the Hecke algebra T^S; Shin's stable Igusa trace formula specialized to G (Corollary 5.2.5, Remark 5.2.6, endoscopic groups G_{n_1,n_2}) and the base-change expression through twisted spectral sides for inner forms of arbitrary signature at ∞ (Theorem 5.3.2), importing ET.4–ET.5 and ET.7b for the transfers, the twisted trace formula and Red^b. (2) The genericity obstruction: Lemma 5.4.3 (generic principal series die under the Langlands–Jacquet map for non-quasi-split J_{b_i}), Lemma 5.5.8 (only the µ-ordinary class of GL_n has quasi-split J_b), Lemma 5.5.1, Corollary 5.5.2, Theorem 5.5.4 (r_i : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_{n_i}(Q̄_ℓ)), Corollary 5.5.5, Remark 5.5.6 and Theorem 5.5.7: for b not µ-ordinary, BC^p([H_c(I^b_Mant, Q̄_ℓ)]^{S-ur})_r = 0. (3) Simple Shimura varieties (§5.6): Proposition 5.6.1, Corollaries 5.6.2–5.6.3, with Matsushima's formula and the stable trace formula for S_K. (4) Lemma 6.2.2 (decomposed generic ⇒ sum of characters, generic principal series) and Theorem 6.3.1: Hochschild–Serre to infinite level at a split p, Leray for π_HT, the minimal Newton stratum (Corollary 6.1.4 from the source route), Poincaré duality with the dual Hecke ideal. Record as an expectation, not a target, Remark 1.18: Rπ_HT*Q̄_ℓ should be the pullback along Fℓ_{G,µ} → Bun_G of Fargues' conjectural perverse sheaves.

Import, never re-plan: IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.0–IG.4 (central leaves, Igusa varieties, Rapoport–Zink spaces, the product formula and Theorem 4.4.4, perversity and Corollary 6.1.4, in the general compact PEL form added by this paper's source route); Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison) ET.0–ET.7b; Automorphic Galois Representations PartII (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII) AG2.0, AG2.2, AG2.5; Reductive bundles, B(G) and Newton strata (BunGAndNewtonStrata) BG0–BG3 (with the flag-variety Newton strata of this paper's source route); Shimura towers and perfectoid representability (PerfectoidShimuraVarieties) S1–S3; Hodge–Tate theory, canonical subgroups, and automorphic period maps (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups) T0–T2; Siegel and PEL moduli problems (PELModuli) M1–M2; Global Galois duality and compact coefficients (ArithmeticGaloisDuality) R02.2; Étale duality, cycle classes and perverse sheaves (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves) EDC.2:pairings. Prerequisites: Shin's three papers (Duke 2009, JIMJ 2010, Ann. of Math. 2011), Scholze's 'On torsion' (Ann. of Math. 2015), Mantovan (Duke 2005). Tests: the modular curve (Fℓ = P^1(Q_p) ⊔ Ω^2), a Harris–Taylor signature (1, n − 1), a nonsplit inner form of GL_5 with µ = (1,1,0,0,0) and Lemma 5.5.8 for n = 2.
routes.reason: IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration plans the Igusa-variety route to torsion concentration only for the non-compact quasi-split datum of the sequel, and says its constructions assert nothing for other data. The compact theorem needs new layers in the same direction: Shin's trace formula with unitary endoscopy for inner forms of arbitrary signature, the genericity obstruction on non-µ-ordinary strata, simple Shimura varieties and the concentration theorem. The geometry itself is added to IG.0–IG.4 by the source route, so the Part II only imports it.

IG.0–IG.4 plan central leaves, the automorphism group of a PEL p-divisible group, Igusa towers, the fibres of the Hodge–Tate period map and nearby-cycle semiperversity, and IG.1 already names CS17 §4 as a source; they do so for the sequel's split unitary datum. CS17 proves the same statements for arbitrary compact PEL data of type (A)/(C) with good reduction: Chai–Oort's internal Hom, Rapoport–Zink spaces of PEL type at infinite level with the local period map to Fℓ^b and the structure of Aut_G(X̃_b), the dimension of Fℓ^b, the perfect Igusa variety and the product formula, Theorem 4.4.4, equivariant sites, Proposition 6.1.3 and Corollary 6.1.4. The geometry keeps one owner if these layers are blueprinted in that generality.

BG2–BG3 own |Bun_G| → B(G), the semicontinuity of ν and the Newton strata. The Newton stratification of the flag variety (Definition 3.5.6, Proposition 3.5.7, Corollary 3.5.9 = Theorem 1.11) is its pullback along Fℓ_{G,µ} ≅ Gr_{G,µ} → Bun_G, and Lemmas 3.5.4–3.5.5, Proposition 3.5.3 and Rapoport's Remark 3.5.8 say which classes modifications of type µ reach; no layer states them.

GS0:Schubert-smoothness identifies a Schubert cell by its parabolic flag base and unipotent fibres; for minuscule µ the fibres are trivial, and Theorem 3.4.5 with Lemmas 3.4.4 and 3.4.6 is that isomorphism Gr^{B_dR^+}_{G,µ} ≅ Fℓ_{G,µ}, proved through Scholze's B^+_dR-local systems.

P8 owns the relative period sheaves and the proper-smooth comparison with connection (Scholze's Theorem 8.8 and Proposition 7.9, planned items here). Corollary 2.2.4 and Proposition 2.2.5 extract from them the relative Hodge–Tate filtration of R^iπ_*Ẑ_p ⊗ Ô_S in every degree; HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T2 uses only its degree-one abelian case.

T0 extends the p-divisible-group API to generic-fibre Tate modules and T2 owns the Hodge–Tate sequence and period maps. Scholze–Weinstein's theory used throughout §4 belongs with them: universal covers and their representability, the classification of p-divisible groups over O_C by (T, W) with the quasi-logarithm, and p-divisible groups over O_C/p as bundles with slopes in [0, 1].
